modules.title: Base Styling & Theme Layout
modules.learningObjective: Implement dark-mode aesthetics using CSS variables and flexbox layouts.
modules.lesson:
CSS variables, also known as custom properties, allow you to define reusable values throughout your stylesheet. By declaring them in the :root pseudo-class, you create a global theme that can be easily updated, such as switching between dark and light modes. This keeps your design consistent and maintainable.

For example, you can define a color variable like this: :root { --main-color: #3498db; } and use it later: .button { background-color: var(--main-color); }.

modules.lesson:
Building a functional user interface requires a clear structure of input elements that allow users to interact with your application. By using semantic HTML tags like <input> and <select>, you create predictable entry points for data, which can then be captured and processed by your JavaScript logic. Think of these elements as the bridge between the user's intent and your code's execution.

For example, to create a simple text input, you would use: <input type='text' id='username' placeholder='Enter name'>. This element provides a standard way for users to type information, which you can later access in your scripts using document.getElementById('username').value.

modules.title: Core JavaScript Logic & Event Handling
modules.learningObjective: Develop the core calculation engine and handle user interaction events to drive dynamic UI updates.
modules.lesson: JavaScript event handling allows your application to respond to user interactions in real-time. By attaching listeners to inputs and buttons, you can trigger functions that process data, perform calculations, and update the DOM dynamically without reloading the page. This creates a seamless, app-like experience for the user. For example, you can listen for a 'click' event on a button to toggle a CSS class: document.querySelector('.btn').addEventListener('click', () => document.body.classList.toggle('dark-mode'));
modules.task:

solutionFiles.content: const rates = { USD: 1.0, EUR: 0.92, GBP: 0.79, JPY: 155.2, CAD: 1.38 }; const amountInput = document.getElementById('amount-input'); const fromCurrency = document.getElementById('from-currency'); const toCurrency = document.getElementById('to-currency'); const swapBtn = document.getElementById('swap-btn'); const rateDisplay = document.getElementById('rate-display'); const resultDisplay = document.getElementById('result-display'); function calculateConversion() { const amount = parseFloat(amountInput.value) || 0; const from = fromCurrency.value; const to = toCurrency.value; const rate = (rates[to] / rates[from]); const result = (amount * rate).toFixed(2); rateDisplay.textContent = `1 ${from} = ${rate.toFixed(4)} ${to}`; resultDisplay.textContent = `${result} ${to}`; } function swapCurrencies() { const temp = fromCurrency.value; fromCurrency.value = toCurrency.value; toCurrency.value = temp; calculateConversion(); } amountInput.addEventListener('input', calculateConversion); fromCurrency.addEventListener('change', calculateConversion); toCurrency.addEventListener('change', calculateConversion); swapBtn.addEventListener('click', swapCurrencies); calculateConversion();

modules.title: State Persistence & Final Integration
modules.learningObjective: Implement browser LocalStorage to save and render user conversion history for a complete experience.
modules.lesson: State persistence allows your web application to remember user data even after a page refresh. By using the browser's LocalStorage API, you can store key-value pairs as strings, enabling a seamless experience where user history or preferences remain intact between sessions. Always remember to use JSON.stringify() when saving objects and JSON.parse() when retrieving them to ensure data integrity. A quick example of storing a simple preference: localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');.

solutionFiles.content: const rates = { USD: 1.0, EUR: 0.92, GBP: 0.79, JPY: 155.2, CAD: 1.38 }; const amountInput = document.getElementById('amount-input'); const fromCurrency = document.getElementById('from-currency'); const toCurrency = document.getElementById('to-currency'); const swapBtn = document.getElementById('swap-btn'); const rateDisplay = document.getElementById('rate-display'); const resultDisplay = document.getElementById('result-display'); const historyList = document.getElementById('history-list'); const STORAGE_KEY = 'currency_converter_history_v1'; function calculateConversion() { const amount = parseFloat(amountInput.value) || 0; const from = fromCurrency.value; const to = toCurrency.value; const rate = (rates[to] / rates[from]); const result = (amount * rate).toFixed(2); rateDisplay.textContent = `1 ${from} = ${rate.toFixed(4)} ${to}`; resultDisplay.textContent = `${result} ${to}`; if (amount > 0) { saveToHistory(`${amount} ${from} → ${result} ${to}`); } } function saveToHistory(entry) { try { const history = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) || '[]'); const updated = [entry, ...history.filter(h => h !== entry)].slice(0, 5); localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(updated)); renderHistory(); } catch (e) { console.warn('LocalStorage error:', e); } } function renderHistory() { try { const history = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) || '[]'); historyList.innerHTML = ''; history.forEach(item => { const li = document.createElement('li'); li.textContent = item; historyList.appendChild(li); }); } catch (e) { console.warn('Failed to render history:', e); } } function swapCurrencies() { const temp = fromCurrency.value; fromCurrency.value = toCurrency.value; toCurrency.value = temp; calculateConversion(); } amountInput.addEventListener('input', calculateConversion); fromCurrency.addEventListener('change', calculateConversion); toCurrency.addEventListener('change', calculateConversion); swapBtn.addEventListener('click', swapCurrencies); calculateConversion(); renderHistory();
